related_questions.snippet: Thiamine is used to treat beriberi (tingling and numbness in feet and hands, muscle loss, and poor reflexes caused by a lack of thiamine in the diet) and to treat and prevent Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome (tingling and numbness in hands and feet, memory loss, confusion caused by a lack of thiamine in the diet).

related_questions.question: Why would a doctor prescribe thiamine?
related_questions.snippet: Vitamin B1 helps the cells in the body convert food into energy. If you do not have enough vitamin B1 this process cannot work properly. You may have symptoms such as tiredness, loss of appetite and muscle weakness. Taking a thiamine supplement helps restore normal levels of vitamin B1 in your body.

related_questions.question: Why do we give thiamine to alcoholics?

text_blocks.snippet: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) is given to alcoholics to prevent and treat Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome (WKS), a serious brain disorder caused by thiamine deficiency, which is common in individuals with alcohol use disorder. Alcoholics are susceptible to thiamine deficiency due to poor nutrition and impaired thiamine absorption caused by alcohol consumption.
snippet_highlighted_words: to prevent and treat Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome (WKS)

text_blocks.snippet: Here's why thiamine is crucial for alcoholics:

list.title: Preventing Wernicke-Korsakoff Syndrome:
list.snippet: WKS has two stages: Wernicke's encephalopathy (acute phase) and Korsakoff's psychosis (chronic phase). Wernicke's encephalopathy can cause confusion, eye movement problems, and difficulty with muscle coordination, while Korsakoff's psychosis can lead to severe memory loss and impaired cognitive function. Thiamine supplementation can prevent or reverse the symptoms of Wernicke's encephalopathy, especially if treated early.

list.title: Addressing Nutritional Deficiency:
list.snippet: Alcoholics often have poor dietary intake and impaired absorption of nutrients, including thiamine. Alcohol also interferes with thiamine's absorption in the gut. Giving thiamine helps correct this deficiency and supports overall health.

list.title: Managing Alcohol Withdrawal:
list.snippet: During alcohol withdrawal, the body's demand for thiamine increases, making supplementation even more important. Thiamine can help mitigate the effects of withdrawal and support the body's recovery.

list.title: Reversing Neurological Damage:
list.snippet: In some cases, Wernicke's encephalopathy can be reversed with prompt and adequate thiamine treatment. Early intervention is key to minimizing the risk of permanent brain damage.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary, thiamine is administered to alcoholics to prevent and treat the severe neurological consequences of thiamine deficiency, a common complication of alcohol abuse, and to support their overall nutritional status.
